subject: SKU shelf pricing harmonization + distributor rebate routing
messages:
From: Sara Liao <sara.liao@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Reed <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify SKU shelf pricing across AWS/GCP + distributor rebate routing

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are starting the procurement run for the 2028 subscription and need clarification on two items before we move to PO: 1) whether the list/shelf price we publish in the marketplace will be unified across AWS and GCP (Acme wants a single customer-facing price) and 2) how distributor/re-seller rebates will be routed and reflected on our invoice (we operate through a regional distributor).

Attached is a short summary of our estimated SKU mix and volumes (acme_po_summary.pdf). High-level asks: can you confirm if Redwood can (a) publish the same list price for both clouds while honoring platform-specific private-offer discounts and (b) route distributor rebates via the private offer so they appear as an invoice deduction (we need distributor-friendly documentation for our Finance team)? If needed we can loop in the AWS marketplace contact (cc'd).

Target timeline: we are trying to finalize commercial terms by July 12th. Let me know if a short call makes sense.

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Procurement
Acme Health

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ethan Reed <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SKU shelf pricing across AWS/GCP + distributor rebate routing

Sara — really appreciate the note and the attachment. Short answers up front: yes, we can display a harmonized list price across clouds while applying cloud-specific private-offer discounts; and yes, we can route distributor rebates via the private offer with invoice-level deduction if we coordinate the reseller ID and payment routing ahead of the PO.

That said, there are two operational options depending on how Acme wants to treat the rebate visibility and tax handling:

Option A — Unified list price with private-offer overlay: Redwood publishes a single public shelf price tied to the SKU family. For Acme we provision cloud-specific private offers (AWS/GCP) that apply the negotiated discount. Distributor rebates are modelled as an invoice deduction routed by the marketplace partner (we will need the distributor's marketplace account ID and remit instructions). This keeps reporting simple for Acme but requires marketplace routing setup.

Option B — Platform-specific shelf price + distributor-managed rebate: Publish platform-specific list prices that reflect platform fees. Distributor rebate is handled off-invoice by the distributor (we issue full invoice; distributor sends back rebate separately). This reduces marketplace routing work but creates extra reconciliation for Acme Finance.

Next steps I propose: 1) We do a 30-minute call with your Finance + distributor ops to capture the distributor account IDs and tax treatment; 2) Redwood will produce a short ops diagram and a pricing matrix showing final customer price, private-offer discount, and distributor rebate waterfall. I've attached a draft pricing matrix (redwood_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx) for internal review.

If you prefer, Vanessa and Ben can join to walk the ops flow. Are you available Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

— Vivek
Head of Market Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify SKU shelf pricing across AWS/GCP + distributor rebate routing

FYI — forwarding Sara's note. Quick thoughts below; feel free to add redlines before I send back to Vivek/Sara.

On Thu, 01 Jul 2027 at 11:05, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sara — really appreciate the note and the attachment. Short answers up front: yes, we can display a harmonized list price across clouds while applying cloud-specific private-offer discounts; and yes, we can route distributor rebates via the private offer with invoice-level deduction if we coordinate the reseller ID and payment routing ahead of the PO.

Notes: 
- Ops: we'll need distributor marketplace account ID (AWS seller ID or GCP reseller ID) + W-9 / tax docs to set up pass-through credits properly.
- Margin: if we route rebates on-invoice the reseller shows a netback that will make our gross recognized revenue lower; need to reflect in the deal waterfall and revenue ops mapping. Recommend we propose a 2% ops handling fee (one-time) to cover routing complexity unless Acme takes Option B.
- Legal: require explicit language in the PO that rebates routed via marketplace are applied as invoice credit and not as a separate vendor rebate. Ask Irene to draft the clause.

Ben — can you run margin sims (netback) for both Option A and B across the attached matrix? Week-on-week velocity assumptions: see tab "Q3 Mix".

Vanessa
Director, Channel GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SKU shelf pricing across AWS/GCP + distributor rebate routing

All — ran the sims and attached an ops diagram (ops_rebate_flow.drawio exported as PNG in the multi-file bundle). Summary:
- Option A (marketplace invoice-credit): Expected Redwood net revenue -6.1% on nominal FY28 ARR due to distributor pass-through; variance range +/-1.2% depending on SKU mix.
- Option B (off-invoice distributor rebate): Redwood net revenue -2.8% but Acme Finance will have a more complex reconciliation (distributor pays rebate after invoice).

Recommendation: propose Option A to the customer but include an override path in the PO that allows Option B for regions where distributor routing can't be supported. Also propose a one-time 2% ops handling fee to cover marketplace routing setup and verifying tax docs.

Irene — can you draft the PO language for Option A (marketplace invoice credit) + the fallback clause? I'll include the margin sims in the deck for Sara.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Final email (to Acme):
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liao <sara.liao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ethan Reed <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed approach: harmonized shelf price + marketplace rebate routing (Option A)

Sara — thanks for the patience. Based on internal ops/margin review we've put together a preferred approach and a fallback (summary below) and attached an ops diagram and the margin sims for your Finance team.

Summary (preferred):
- Publish a harmonized public shelf price for the SKU family across AWS and GCP.
- Redwood will create cloud-specific private offers that apply the negotiated discount so Acme sees a single contracted customer price.
- Distributor rebate will be routed as an invoice credit via the marketplace partner (requires distributor marketplace account ID and completed tax documentation).
- One-time ops handling fee: 2% of first-year committed ARR to cover routing/tax set-up. This is optional; if Acme prefers off-invoice handling we will document the reconciliation differences.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx, ops_rebate_flow.drawio (PNG).

Next steps: If this matches Acme's preference, please confirm and we'll: 1) collect distributor marketplace IDs and tax docs, 2) circulate the PO language (Irene + legal), and 3) schedule a 30-min handoff call with AWS marketplace ops (Ethan) to finalize routing.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Market Partnerships
Redwood Inference
